parts.text: In this experiment, you will compare the resistances of two wires. The circuit has been set up for you. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Connect the crocodile clip to a length l = 90.0 cm of resistance wire A. Close the switch. Measure, and record in Table 2.1, the value of potential difference (p.d.) V and current I for the wire. Open the switch. Calculate, and record in Table 2.1, the resistance R of 90.0 cm of wire A. Use your values of V and I and the equation R = V I . [3] Table 2.1 wire l / cm V / I / R / A 90.0 B 90.0 A 50.0 B 50.0

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text:
V all < 3.0 V
I all < 1.00 A
All V to at least 1dp and all I to at least 2dp

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) Repeat step (a) for l = 90.0 cm of wire B, l = 50.0 cm of wire A and l = 50.0 cm of wire B. [2]

ms.label: 2(b)(i)
ms.text:
correct calculations of R
R consistent 2 or 3 significant figures

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Calculate a value P using your results from Table 2.1 and the equation P = R for 90.0 cm of wire A R for 90.0 cm of wire B . P = .......................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a value Q using your results from Table 2.1 and the equation Q = R for 50.0 cm of wire A R for 50.0 cm of wire B . Q = .......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(c)(iii)
ms.text:
statement matching results and values used
justification matching statement
e.g. within limits of experimental accuracy / owtte

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
valid inherent source of inaccuracy
e.g: crocodile clip connection not even / difficult to connect at exactly the correct length / resistance wires not uniform
